newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, led by silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, led by silver.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Wednesday, led by a sharp fall in silver, although volume remained moderate.

"The whole complex continues to erode, with silver rotting on the vine," FIMAT trader John Tyree said. "Locals and the trade lent on silver heavily but there may be some support around $4.68 (for December delivery)."

COMEX December silver ended down 8.0 cents at $4.713 an ounce after seeing an intraday low at $4.710. Total estimated volume in silver futures were 13,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot silver saw a fresh 18-month low of $4.72.
COMEX December gold closed down $0.90 at $378.70 after seeing a session low at $378.30, but December gold remains above the contract low at $377.70 set Oct 31.

In the bullion market, spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted at $377.70/378.20 versus the London afternoon fix at $378.00, and the New York close Tuesday at $378.50/379.00, but above the 19-month low of $376.80 seen last week.
The spot gold/silver ratio jumped to a fresh 19 month high at 80.0.
The further rally in the U.S. bond market, following President Clinton's re-election as president Tuesday, was discouraging investors in precious metals, traders said.
Meanwhile, continued strength in the dollar, particularly against yen, was dampening fabricator demand in Asia.
Investment demand accounts for about 23 percent of the movement in the price of gold, in CPM Group's econometric model for forecasting gold prices, while jewelry demand accounts for about 39 pct.

Total open interest in COMEX gold futures has risen again in the past few days to 192,814 lots on Monday, as gold has slipped lower, though funds already have a record net short position, according to the CFTC Commitment of Traders data.
COMEX silver open interest has also been edging back up, standing at 96,405 lots Monday.

The December 1996/April 1997 gold contango ended at $4.00 an ounce Wednesday, from $5.20 in early September, while the December 1996/March 1997 spread ended at 6.700 cents, down from 8.400 cents in July.

"The narrowing of the spreads suggests a bearish outlook by producers, hedging their forward output, which means the downtrend is probably not going to reverse anytime soon," Refco's New York analyst James Steel said.
The 12-month December 1996/December 1997 gold contango also fell to nine month lows at $13.30 on November 1, before recovering a little to close at $13.50 an ounce Wednesday, traders said.
NYMEX January platinum closed down $1.20 at $382.80 after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low of $382.00, while NYMEX December palladium ended $1.70 lower at $116.25.
In the bullion market, platinum posted a 35-month low of $378.25 last Friday, while palladium set a 43-month low of $114.00 last Thursday.
The April gold/platinum spread slipped back to $2.70 at the close, after recovering partially from a slide to zero in late October.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
